fields.title: The Missing Laptop
fields.description:
A laptop belonging to the college computer lab has disappeared. It was last seen on a desk at 2:20 PM.

Four students were in or around the lab that afternoon: Umra, Bushra, Ariz, and Maseera.

The laptop was discovered missing at 3:00 PM.

The lab's security camera stopped recording between 2:20 PM and 2:30 PM because of a temporary power problem.

Umra said that she left the lab at 2:10 PM and went directly to the cafeteria.

Bushra said that she stayed in the lab until 2:45 PM because she was working on her assignment.

Ariz said that he left the lab at 2:15 PM because he had a lecture at 2:30 PM.

Maseera said that she was in the lab until 3:00 PM but never touched the laptop.

Evidence 1: Umra's cafeteria receipt is timestamped 2:18 PM.

Evidence 2: The attendance system shows Bushra attending a lecture in Room 204 at 2:30 PM.

Evidence 3: Ariz's lecturer confirms that Ariz was present in the lecture from 2:25 PM onwards.

Evidence 4: The security camera was not recording between 2:20 PM and 2:30 PM.

Your task is to examine the statements and evidence and determine who is most likely responsible for the missing laptop.

fields.title: The Missing Examination Paper
fields.description:
At 4:30 PM, a sealed envelope containing the next day's examination paper was placed inside the examination office. The office was locked at 5:00 PM.

At 5:20 PM, the principal discovered that the envelope was missing.

There was no sign of forced entry.

Four people were known to be near the examination office that evening.

Rahul, the office assistant, said that he left the building at 4:50 PM. His attendance record shows that he scanned his ID at the main gate at 4:52 PM.

Neha, a teacher, said that she went to the staff room at 4:45 PM and remained there until 5:30 PM. Another teacher confirmed seeing her in the staff room at 5:10 PM.

Amit, the computer technician, said that he entered the examination office at 5:05 PM to repair a computer. He claimed that the office was already locked and that he left immediately.

Priya, the clerk, said that she was preparing documents in the administration room and never went near the examination office.

However, CCTV shows Priya walking toward the examination office at 5:02 PM and returning toward the administration room at 5:08 PM.

The electronic door record shows that the examination office was opened at 5:03 PM. The office computer also recorded a print at 5:04 PM.

Your task is to examine the timeline, compare the statements with the evidence, eliminate suspects who could not have committed the crime, and determine who was most likely responsible for the missing examination paper.

fields.title: The Diamond That Wasn't Stolen
fields.description:
At 8:45 PM, a priceless diamond disappears from a locked display case inside the city's most secure museum. There are no broken locks, no fingerprints on the glass, and the alarm never went off.

Four people were present in the museum that evening, and each gives a convincing account of their movements.

The security system shows that the display case was opened during a short period when the alarm had been disabled for routine maintenance. However, one piece of evidence suggests that the diamond may have disappeared long before anyone realized it was missing.

Your task is to reconstruct the timeline, examine the evidence carefully, identify the contradiction in the suspects' statements, and determine how the diamond disappeared�and who was responsible.

fields.title: The Vanishing Blueprint
fields.description:
At 7:00 PM, a confidential architectural blueprint was placed inside a locked cabinet in the design department.

At 8:30 PM, the chief architect returned and discovered that the blueprint had disappeared.

There was no damage to the cabinet or signs of forced entry.

Four employees were still inside the building that evening.

Arjun, the security guard, claimed he remained at the main entrance from 7:00 PM until 8:30 PM.

Meera, an architect, said she left the building at 7:15 PM.

Rohan, the IT technician, claimed he was fixing a printer on the second floor between 7:20 PM and 8:00 PM.

Sara, the project assistant, said she spent the entire evening in the conference room preparing documents.

However, the building's access system recorded that Sara's access card was used to enter the design department at 7:42 PM.

Security footage shows Rohan passing the design department at 7:45 PM, despite claiming he was on the second floor.

The cabinet was opened at 7:43 PM.

fields.title: The 11:47 Photograph
fields.description:
At exactly 11:47 PM, a photograph was uploaded to the private account of a famous journalist, Daniel Cross.

The photograph showed Daniel standing outside an abandoned railway station.

There was only one problem.

Daniel had been reported dead three hours earlier.

Police had already identified his body at his apartment at 8:32 PM.

His phone was found beside him.

The account was protected by a password known only to Daniel.

At first, investigators believed the photograph had been scheduled in advance.

But the photograph contained something unexpected.
In the background was a digital railway clock displaying:

11:46 PM

Investigators checked the station's records.

The station had been abandoned for six years.

Four people had a possible connection to Daniel that night:

Maya, his editor, claimed she spoke to Daniel on the phone at 7:45 PM and left the city at 8:00 PM.

Arjun, his photographer, claimed Daniel had asked him to meet at the railway station at 10:30 PM, but Arjun never went because he believed Daniel was already dead.
Kabir, Daniel's brother, claimed he was at home all evening.

Nisha, a technology consultant, said she had helped Daniel secure his online accounts two weeks earlier but had not spoken to him since.

Investigators discovered that the photograph had been uploaded at 11:47 PM.

The railway clock in the photograph showed 11:46 PM.

But there was another problem.

The railway station had no electricity.

And the clock had not worked for six years.

Someone had deliberately created the photograph.

Your task is to determine why the photograph was created, who could have created it, and what the photograph was actually meant to prove.
